newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Shell says price hike not to affect sales.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Shell says price hike not to affect sales.

text.p: Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp said on Thursday that it expects to maintain its existing market share despite an increase in petroleum prices.

"I don't think it will affect our market share. The growth of the economy still remains robust and we hope the period of uncertainty on the peso is over," said Pilipinas Shell general manager for corporate affairs Reynaldo Gamboa.
Pilipinas Shell announced it was raising wholesale petroleum product prices by an average of 23 centavos a litre effective August 1.
It was the first of the three local oil refiners to announce an increase in petroleum product prices after the peso was effectively devalued more than two weeks ago.
Gamboa said Pilipinas Shell which has 37 percent of the Philippine petroleum market will likely keep or improve its market share during the rest of the year.
"We aim to be the leading marketer and competition was a major factor in the price adjustments," said Gamboa.

"We tried to lessen the impact on socially-sensitive products like diesel which is used for public transportation, fuel oil for power and liquefied petroleum gas used by households so as not to be inflationary," Gamboa said.
He said as a rule of thumb a one peso depreciation compared to the dollar should translate to a 14.5 centavo per litre increase in the landed cost of crude.
The dollar has been hovering at 28.50 to 29 pesos compared to the 26.4 peso level before the currency was allowed to float in a wider range.
Gamboa said Shell had not passed on the entire additional cost of the peso's depreciation.
Pilipinas Shell is a member of the Royal Dutch/Shell group of companies.
